title: Ask the supplier only for prices the shop doesn't have

blocks.text: A web shop prices its basket through `PriceBook`. Prices the shop has on file come from a map; for anything else it asks the supplier's quote service, a slow remote call the supplier bills per request. Buyers add products the shop has never listed, and the catalogue team lists new products before their price is settled.
`PriceBook` already stores the listings. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/PriceBook.java`:

items: `price(sku)`: the price on file for a product, if it has one;
`priceOrQuote(sku)`: the price on file, or else the supplier's quote.

blocks.text: When you're done, any product a buyer can name gets an answer without an exception, and the supplier's bill shows a request only for products whose price isn't on file. About two lines in total.

cases.says: a product with a price on file has that price, from price(...) and from priceOrQuote(...)
a product the shop never listed has an empty price, without an exception, and priceOrQuote asks the supplier for it
a product listed before it has a price has an empty price, without an exception, and priceOrQuote asks the supplier for it
priceOrQuote makes no request to the supplier for a product whose price is on file

origin.section: Put Absence in the Return Type: an Empty Optional or an Empty Collection, Never null

concepts: A value that may be missing is returned as an Optional built with ofNullable, since Optional.of throws on null and a bare null fails at the caller.
Optional.orElse evaluates its argument whether or not a value is present; orElseGet calls its supplier only when the Optional is empty.
